item.title: Pat Fitzgerald basks in U-M win, shifts MSU's focus to Washington
item.description: EAST LANSING – They only count as one, even if Pat Fitzgerald immediately admitted “there’s one game that just means a little bit more” when he took the Michigan State football job. The Spartans got that one and the Paul Bunyan Trophy . And after his congratulatory messages with Mark Dantonio following Saturday’s win at Michigan and a lengthy phone call with Dantonio on Sunday, MSU’s first-year coach Fitzgerald knows one more thing. How you follow an emotional victory over the rival Wolverines can change a season. For good or bad. Especially now that his team has given itself new life for a seemingly improbable bowl berth with the Washington Huskies coming to town. I mean, we all know that that win gave us an opportunity and the right to have this be a big game this weekend if that makes sense,” Fitzgerald said at his news conference Monday, Nov. 9. “That’s the way I approach it with the guys. This is a critical game for this team.” Needing to win all three of its remaining games to qualify for a postseason spot, MSU (3-6, 1-5 Big Ten) begins the final quarter of the season by hosting Washington (5-4, 2-4) and quarterback Demond Williams Jr., a Spartan legacy, on Saturday (4:15 p.m., Big Ten Network). The Spartans have a short week after facing the Huskies , hosting Oregon in their home finale on Friday Nov. 20, before traveling to Rutgers on Nov. 28 to close out their 12 regular-season games. “I said, ‘Listen, then that creates next week. item.title: CFP bracket prediction clears up in college football bowl projections after Week 10
item.description: The Week 10 lineup in college football was always going to have a major impact on the College Football Playoff due to it being stacked with ranked matchups. And the results from last weekend didn't disappoint in causing the predictions for the field in this week's week bowl projections to have a new look. It was a great day for three teams. Tennessee with its dominant defeat of Kentucky was a second huge home win for the Volunteers in their chase to make the 12-team field. Iowa , meanwhile, got an important road win at Northwestern to boost its resume, and Wake Forest benefitted from losses by contenders Ohio State, Brigham Young, LSU and Mississippi. The Hawkeyes and Demon Deacons are now squarely in position to win their way in but will still need some good fortune. The news wasn't as good for those contenders that fell Saturday. The Buckeyes and Cougars still can reach their respective conference title games. A bunch of results will need to go their way, however. The Tigers and Rebels don't have much hope after their third losses. That said, anything can happen over these next four weeks. There are tons of imperfect teams and unexpected results are certain. It's an unenviable task coming for the committee on Selection Sunday, but there seems to be more sense of where this is going. item.title: Arsenal 31yo makes World 11, teammate narrowly misses out
item.description: Arsenal 31yo makes World 11, teammate narrowly misses out David Raya has become the first Arsenal player to feature in the FIFPRO World 11 since Thierry Henry, with a couple of his teammates only narrowly missing out. Photo via FIFPRO on Instagram After tallying up 19,806 votes from professional men’s footballers across 73 countries, FIFPRO named their World 11 on Monday night, with Arsenal’s David Raya making the cut. Raya is the first Arsenal player to be included in the World 11 since Thierry Henry in 2006, and he’s one of just two Premier League players in the 2026 side alongside Erling Haaland (or three if you include Rodri ). It wasn’t a close race in the goalkeeper position, with Raya receiving more than 2,500 more votes than his nearest competitor. In fact, the goalkeeper received more votes than anyone else in the entire lineup, with over half of the voters picking him. FIFPRO World 11 for 2026 Arsenal were rather unlucky not to have at least one more player in the lineup. Gabriel Magalhaes received the second-most votes of any centre-back, only behind Pau Cubarsi of Barcelona and Spain. But the award organisers opted to select a team with only three defenders, one of whom was a left-back, and another a right-back. So with only one centre-back spot in the side, Gabriel missed out. If the team used a formation that a real football team might use, Gabriel would have been included, as it’s very hard to think of any team in world football that only uses one centre-back. William Saliba was also very close to making the cut, as both Gabriel and Saliba finished within 1,000 votes of Cubarsi. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Declan Rice was the other Arsenal player to receive a significant quantity of votes, but he wasn’t particularly close to making the final team. Though he received over 3,000 votes, that was around 2,500 short of anyone in the top-three. Raya sent a message to the voters after receiving his award, saying : “Thank you guys for voting me into the FIFPRO World 11. It’s incredible how you guys have voted for me. Thank you very much to everyone that has chosen me to be part of this, and keep doing your thing.” Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

item.title: ‘Y’all wish’ – Luka Doncic responds to Atlanta Hawks heckler with reminder their biggest mistake
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Even eight years later, Luka Doncic has not forgotten about how the Atlanta Hawks disrespected him in the NBA Draft. Doncic is now the next superstar for the Los Angeles Lakers, taking over the mantle from LeBron James following his departure earlier this summer. But before he arrived in Los Angeles, Doncic was the name and face of the Dallas Mavericks for seven years, a position carved out for him on the night of the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic pokes fun at Atlanta Hawks fan over 2018 NBA Draft trade During the Los Angeles Lakers’ win against the Atlanta Hawks, Luka Doncic got into a heated exchange with some hecklers sitting courtside. Doncic used the back-and-forth as an opportunity to remind them that the Hawks made a mistake giving him up in the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic: “You all wish you would’ve had me. You all wish, huh?” Fan #1: “We had you.” Fan #2: “No, we don’t. I’ve never wanted you.” Fan #3: “I wish we did; I do.” Luka Doncic: “You know you could have had me.” Fan #3: “He’s right.” Of course, Doncic is referencing the draft-night trade the Atlanta Hawks made in 2018. The Hawks had the #3 overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft, with Doncic being expected to be selected by the Hawks. However, on the night, the Hawks traded the draft rights to Luka Doncic (whom they picked at #3) to the Dallas Mavericks in exchange for the draft rights to Trae Young and a 2019 protected first-round pick that turned out to be Cam Reddish. Fast-forward eight years, and the Hawks have fully given up on Trae Young, trading him to the Washington Wizards earlier this year after an eight-year stint that saw them reach the Eastern Conference Finals just once. As for Cam Reddish, he never adapted to the NBA and found himself outside of the league following the conclusion of the 2024-25 NBA season. In the early days of the trade, many had suggested that the Mavericks and Hawks had pulled off a rare win-win trade. However, following Young’s decline as a superstar, the consensus became clear – the Mavericks had pulled off a coup for Doncic. Unfortunately for the Mavericks, they didn’t get to reap the rewards of their clever trade, as Nico Harrison would trade Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and just one first-round pick. Now, the Lakers have emerged as the ultimate winners of a trade in 2018 that never included them in the first place. item.title: “It’s Going To Be Like Yoshinobu Yamamoto” – MLB Insider Drops Intriguing Update on Tarik Skubal’s Free Agency Outlook
item.description: Tarik Skubal | © Instagram /@dodgers MLB insider and New York Post columnist Joel Sherman believes Tarik Skubal’s free agency could mirror that of Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who signed the largest pitching contract in MLB history with Los Angeles during the 2023 offseason (12-year, $325 million). Sherman shared his thoughts on the latest episode of ‘The Show’ with co-host Jon Heyman, a fellow MLB insider. Discussing several facets of the ongoing offseason, Sherman began by naming some of the game’s aces before quickly turning to Skubal, saying his free-agent battle could come down to the Mets and Dodgers. Although plenty of teams will be interested in acquiring him, the pursuit could ultimately end much as Yamamoto’s did. “So look, I think they’re, to your point, if we were going to name who’s the ace of the sport, it would be a very short list. Yamamoto, Skubal, maybe Schlittler, like Skubal’s on it, and it might be Skubal, to your point. And he’s free,” Sherman said. “And so I think there’ll be interest in him. And yet I think it’s going to be like Yoshinobu Yamamoto. I think it’s the Mets and the Dodgers. I have yet to talk to an executive or a scout who doesn’t think it’s going to be the Mets versus the Dodgers in this,” he added. Watch the video here: During the campaign’s second half, Skubal and Yamamoto got a taste of what it would be like to team up with another ace. Skubal, the two-time AL Cy Young winner, was traded to LA for three prospects. The two pushed each other and finished the regular season strong. Skubal finished the campaign 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts, and a 0.96 WHIP, while Yamamoto went 14-9 with a 2.53 ERA, 182 strikeouts, and a 0.87 WHIP. During the postseason, Skubal was chosen ahead of Yamamoto to start the NLDS and NLCS openers. Jon Heyman Believes the Mets Are Favorites to Sign Tarik Skubal This Offseason Appearing on MLB Network to share his take on the offseason’s most discussed topic, MLB insider Heyman said he believes the Mets were favorites to land Skubal, potentially dealing a blow to LA. The reasoning is simple: the left-handed ace is unlikely to seek a short-term deal with any team. “I do favor the Mets at this point. We are not exactly sure where the Dodgers are going to go. They are not in the desperation mode that the Mets are in to get better. I think the Mets are the favorite,” Heyman said. Monday was the first day of the General Managers’ meetings in Las Vegas, and multiple sources already believe the Mets are favorites to land Skubal this offseason. ESPN’s Jeff Passan also believes Skubal is expected to make his free agency decision by Dec. 1, before the current CBA expires. item.title: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’
item.description: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’ Kylian Mbappe has wasted little time moving on from his Ballon d’Or disappointment, despite finishing just 28 points behind Harry Kane in the voting. The Real Madrid forward came close to claiming the individual award , but Kane ultimately emerged as the winner. Mbappe has not spoken extensively about the result since the ceremony, with his attention returning to club football. However, France and Real Madrid teammate Ibrahima Konate has offered his insight into how the forward has reacted, suggesting the defeat has not affected his focus or motivation. Konate explains why the defeat hurt Mbappe Konate, who signed for Real Madrid this past summer on a free transfer from Liverpool, suggested that the narrow defeat was particularly difficult for the forward because he believed the award was within his reach. Konate explains why Mbappe was hurt after missing out on the Ballon d’or. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) “He more than deserved the Ballon d’Or, which is why it’s tough for him not to have won it.” The Real Madrid defender added, as per Defensa Central , that “He’s in very good spirits. He’s ready for whatever comes his way and is working hard.” Mbappe answers disappointment with goals Mbappe, on his part, has made a strong start to life after the ceremony. He scored in each of the club’s three subsequent fixtures, finding the net against Racing Santander, AEK Athens and Valencia. Mbappe opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 3-0 victory over Racing, struck in the 3-2 Champions League win against AEK and scored again during the 3-0 success at Valencia. Kylian Mbappe is still enjoying a great run of form. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Notably, the sequence of his form is actually giving him a useful platform for the remainder of the campaign. Rather than allowing the Ballon d’Or result to dominate his season, Mbappe can focus on collective trophies and performances that will influence his next opportunity to win it. UCL success could influence Mbappe’s next Ballon d’Or bid The absence of a major men’s international tournament in 2027 places additional importance on club football in the next Ballon d’Or race. Mbappe will therefore have a significant incentive to help Real Madrid compete for the Champions League and deliver consistently across the season. Indeed, the likes of Lamine Yamal will still be in contention, but if Real Madrid win major trophies under Jose Mourinho, especially the Champions League, Mbappe’s chances of challenging for the Ballon d’Or next year will undoubtedly increase.

item.title: Hungarian federation issues Dominik Szoboszlai update as Liverpool left sweating on his fitness
item.description: Hungarian federation issues Dominik Szoboszlai update as Liverpool left sweating on his fitness The Hungarian FA has issued an update on the fitness of Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. There is an injury concern over the midfielder after he sprained his knee in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola unsure as to whether or not the 26-year-old would be able to represent his country during this international window. The Magyars are away to Georgia this coming Saturday and then host Northern Ireland three days later in what could be a straight shootout for promotion to League A on the final matchday. Szoboszlai decision to be left to the ‘last minute’ On Tuesday, the Hungarian FA published an update via X in which they confirmed that a decision on Szoboszlai won’t be taken until the latest possible opportunity. They stated: ‘Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible. ‘However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute.’ (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Liverpool will need Szoboszlai during frantic fixture period As captain of his country, the 26-year-old will no doubt be striving to prove his fitness in time for the match against Georgia on Saturday, or at least be in a position to play against Northern Ireland. However, those of a Liverpool perspective will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai isn’t risked in either game if he isn’t 100% fit to feature, as he’ll be very much needed at Anfield going into the unforgiving winter schedule. The Reds still have 11 more matches to play in 2026, starting with a grudge fixture at home to Manchester United on Sunday week, and squad depth and rotation will be essential during that hectic period in the run-up to Christmas and New Year’s. Having only recently returned from a thigh issue, Andoni Iraola will be hoping that this doesn’t turn into a season of frequent interruptions for the usually dependable Hungarian, who before this autumn hadn’t missed a game through injury since February 2024 ( Transfermarkt ). Whatever the decision on Szoboszlai might be in the coming days, fingers crossed that he’ll be fully fit and firing in time for the Red Devils’ visit to Anfield in 12 days’ time.

item.title: “There’s No Drama” – Mirra Andreeva Breaks Silence On WTA Finals ‘Diva’ Controversy With Jessica Pegula
item.description: Mirra Andreeva © Instagram/_mirraandreeva_ Mirra Andreeva recently addressed the controversy surrounding Jessica Pegula’s ‘diva’ remark at the WTA Finals after the incident caught fans’ attention. Pegula’s private conversation with her coach Mark Knowles was unknowingly broadcast during a practice session at Indian Wells. The American tennis player was heard making comments about Andreeva and her coach Conchita Martínez. Pegula slammed Andreeva’s on-court behavior, calling her a “diva” who needed to be “humbled.” She also took a swipe at Andreeva’s coach for encouraging the French Open champion’s behavior. “I think she’s a nice girl, but she’s a diva; she needs to be humbled,” Pegula said via Tennis World. During her appearance at the WTA Finals, Andreeva broke her silence on the controversy, saying she appreciated that Pegula approached her just a few hours after the incident to apologize (via Christian Court’s X). “I mean, I really appreciated that she came up to me on the same day. I feel, I think maybe a couple of hours just went by and she, you know, she approached me. I would probably like to keep what she said between her and me, but yeah, I really appreciated that she just came up to me. Obviously, she apologized, so there’s no drama or anything behind it. Now we’re able to laugh about it, so I think that’s the most important.” After being seen off by Coco Gauff, Pegula will face Marta Kostyuk in the next group match at the WTA Finals. Mirra Andreeva opens her WTA Finals campaign with a win over Elina Svitolina Mirra Andreeva made her singles debut at the WTA Finals during the 2026 edition in Indian Wells, California. She saw off Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0. Andreeva saved all six break points she faced and held her serve throughout the match. The clash featured a 12-year-and-229-day age gap between the players, the biggest at the WTA Finals since Venus Williams locked horns with Caroline Garcia in 2017. Andreeva was beaten by Svitolina at the Australian Open earlier this year. After her win over Svitolina, Andreeva reflected on her 2025 Indian Wells quarterfinals win over the Ukrainian, where she dominated 7-5, 6-3. “I was trying to think about was that she beat me in Australia earlier this year,” Andreeva said via Rediff . “I really tried not to think about the match we had last year on these courts. I remember how I was playing when I beat her here, but I knew it would be a tricky match. She’s an amazing player. I’m just very happy I was able to get through the match.” Mirra Andreeva will next face Aryna Sabalenka in the group stage of the WTA Finals. Sabalenka overcame Karolina Muchova 7-6(2), 7-5 at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. item.title: Crazy to…’ – Fans call out Dallas Mavericks after Luka Doncic, Jalen Brunson win NBA honour
item.description: Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images Luka Doncic and Jalen Brunson have been chosen for an NBA honour, and fans think the only losers in the equation are the Dallas Mavericks. Luka Doncic and Jalen Brunson are two of the league’s premier superstars. Doncic has begun this season seemingly wanting to wrap up the MVP race as early as possible, and Brunson is the reigning Finals MVP and the ‘King of New York’. In 2026, it is now hard to imagine that the two were on the same team for four years. The Dallas Mavericks drafted both Doncic and Brunson during the 2018 NBA Draft. item.title: Inter target Calhanoglu renewal by Christmas but wage remains sticking point
item.description: Inter target Calhanoglu renewal by Christmas but wage remains sticking point Inter and Hakan Calhanoglu are working towards a contract renewal, but they still need to agree on wages before he can sign. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via TuttoMercatoWeb , both sides want to continue together, and an agreement could be reached by Christmas if the terms fall into place. The 32-year-old’s current deal runs until June 2027 and pays him around €6.5m net per season. MILAN, ITALY – AUGUST 22: Hakan Calhanoglu of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AC Monza at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on August 22, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Calhanoglu’s Inter contract talks The renewal talks follow a tense few months. During Inter’s pre-season tour of Australia in August, Calhanoglu said he was surprised there had been no talks over an extension. He insisted he was still attached to Milan, Inter and the fans, but said his future was in the club’s hands. He was also reportedly worried that he was no longer seen as central to Inter’s plans, even though Cristian Chivu has backed him throughout and he remains key to the team. MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Hakan Calhanoglu of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team’s second goal from the penalty spot during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Parma Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 10, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The main obstacle is money. Calhanoglu wants a new two-year contract with the salary of a top player. Inter, meanwhile, want to reduce the fixed part of their wage bill, especially for a player of his age who has had recent fitness problems. Talks are now open, and both sides will need to compromise to reach a deal.

item.title: 'Big test' awaits FSU basketball against Florida
item.description: Luke Loucks knows Florida State men's basketball's showdown with No. 1 Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 10, will feel a little bit different. The Seminoles (2-0) have outscored opponents 204-137 in the opening two games of the season, a 113-69 win over FAMU and 91-68 win over Troy, and have garnered positive momentum under second-year head coach Luke Loucks . But facing the Gators, the 2025 national champions and top overall team in the country, will be the litmus test for Loucks and his team, which has NCAA tournament aspirations. Loucks feels it's an opportunity for his team to show it can compete with the best teams in the country. The Gators have won the last five meetings, including a 78-76 win in Gainesville last season, and Loucks knows this game means a lot to the community. "Playing the number one team in your house is always special. I mean, I've been a part of a few of these games as a player. I've coached in a few of these games, obviously playing Duke in the ACC tournament when they were number one last year. Then at the NBA level, obviously, playing in the NBA Finals, there's more juice. You can feel the energy from our guys," Loucks said after practice on Monday, Nov. 9 "They've been working their tail off in practice because they're so excited to get out and compete. There is kind of a balance of you don't want to be so excited that you're undisciplined and you forget to do your job. But that excitement, like they're ready to run through a wall right now, so my job is to manage that, and I'm also excited." The Gators have arguably one of the best front courts in the nation with Alex Condon, Ruben Chinyelu and Thomas Haugh, a potential first-round pick in next summer's NBA draft. The trio all average double figures in points per game, with Haugh's 16.5 a team best, closely followed by Chinyelu with 13.5 and Condon with 11.5. Haugh shoots 50% from deep and will take multiple threes a game while also diving into the paint for touches closer to the rim. He's a glass cleaner with 8.5 rebounds per game, and has three steals and a block this season. Haugh, alongside guards Denzel Aberdeen and Boogie Fland, operate at a high level on offense, and Loucks is aware of what the Gators bring to Tallahassee and the opportunity ahead of his players. "They're tough and they're experienced and that's why they win a lot of games," Loucks said. "To me it's a great opportunity for our guys. We have similar size to them. They're just a little bit more unproven, and what better opportunity than to prove it on the biggest stage." Seminole freshman center Marcis Ponder, who will likely draw the matchup with Condon or Chinyelu, and junior forward Sebastian Ranick, who will likely matchup with Haugh, will have their hands full against the Gator bigs. The LSU Tigers dominated for most of the game, judged from the fact that they trailed only for 10 seconds and even built a lead as large as 55 points at one point during the non-conference matchup. However, an incident between the two teams led to officials being involved, grabbing attention long after the game had ended. Emotions ran high in the second half as both teams turned up the physical intensity. A scuffle posted to X prompted officials to assess technical fouls on Louisiana Tech’s Ethan Blackmon, alongside LSU’s Mo Dioubate and Divine Ugochukwu. Following the stoppage, Dioubate registered consecutive field goal conversions before his disqualification via a fifth personal foul. Shooting 56 percent from the field, LSU secured the victory by restricting the Bulldogs to a season-low 50 points, forcing them into shooting only 32% from the field. The LSU Tigers also punished their opponents’ mistakes, establishing a 38-10 advantage in points off turnovers and a 21-2 margin in fast-break points. The game also provided clarity for the LSU Tigers’ reserve rotation, highlighting productive bench performances from center Michael Ruzic and guard Abdi Bashir Jr. Tensions boiled over on the court between these two rivals. Subscribe to stay across the heated moments and storylines reshaping college basketball. Led by Ruzic and Bashir, LSU’s bench produced 40 points, only slightly trailing Louisiana Tech’s overall team total. Mo Dioubate led the starting five with 15 points, six rebounds, and three steals. Donovan Dent added 12 points and five assists, and Skyy Clark scored nine points and added five steals. Coach Will Wade also shed some light on the team’s bench usage. “Look, we’ve got eight starters; all those guys can start,” Wade said, per the Daily Advertiser. “Those guys can all start for a lot of teams. I thought Divine’s (Ugochukwu) a great finisher. Abdi obviously made four 3s tonight. Ruzic was his normal self. Those guys gave us 40 points, which was huge, but we expect that because we’ve got a lot of depth.” Bashir currently leads the LSU Tigers with 11 made 3-pointers this season. He concluded the Louisiana Tech matchup shooting nearly 40 percent from the three-point range. But he also believes there are others on the team who can add lethality from the deep for this team. “We’re a good three-point shooting team,” Bashir said. “Obviously, we’re so dominant in the paint that we don’t need to rely on 3s, but when we get open looks, we got guys that can knock them down. I believe in Skyy more than anybody else on the team to knock them down. And it’s only a matter of time before he goes like 6-for-6 from deep in one game.” LSU’s 40-point victories over New Orleans, Texas Southern, and a Sun Belt opponent provide limited value for its hopes of going deep this season. item.description: Vanderbilt's Chase Nevins pumps his fist after making a birdie putt on the 18th green to win the 49th Palmetto Amateur in 2024. He is one of the top players in this year's field. Play begins Friday, Nov. 13 at Palmetto Golf Club. The 54-hole tournament will end on Sunday, Nov. 15. Spectators are encouraged to attend, and entry is free. Tee times are expected from 8:30-10:30 a.m. each day. This is the second year the event has been played in the fall after being a summer tournament for the past five decades. The field of 78 players features a mix of junior and college-age golfers, mid-amateurs (ages 25-54) and senior amateurs (55 and up). “Last year we switched from summer to fall, and we changed the format,” tournament co-chairman Eric Boetsch said. “In the past we had an open amateur tournament, and most participants were college age. “It was a lot of cool dynamics, seeing some really good college players getting waxed by some really good senior amateur players. item.title: Women’s Sports Drawing Same Audience as Men’s Leagues in Aggregate
item.description: Editor’s Note: JaneWallStreet’s Female Front Office Forum is Thursday! We’re bringing together a curated room of owners, operators and investors —male and female— for a half day of candid conversation and peer-to-peer learning. The sessions will cover audience growth, the evolving sports-capital landscape, and club membership programs. We’ll also dive into women’s sports and how sports properties can better understand and serve female fans. Senior executives interested in joining us can express interest here . We’re expecting the room to be at capacity. Women’s Sports Drawing Same Audience as Men’s Leagues in Aggregate Women’s sports properties often claim to have a differentiated audience than their male counterparts. “There is something incredibly special about women’s football, and it also has a very different audience from men’s football,” former Arsenal CEO Vinai Venkatesham said at UEFA’s Business Case for Women’s Football event in May 2024. Outgoing WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert expressed a similar sentiment in a July 2025 interview with NBC Sports Bay Area . “We are obviously more diverse. We have more women fans, more families, kids,” she said. Engelbert noted that just 4% of Golden State Valkyries season-ticket holders had previously owned Golden State Warriors season tickets as evidence. But that framing is incorrect, and certain to lead to incorrect decisions being made. "[Most people] think about and talk about fandom as if it's vertical. [They view] NBA fans as distinct from WNBA fans as distinct from NFL fans; [separate] cohorts, unique groups of people,” Ben Valenta (EVP, strategy and analytics, Fox Sports) said. However, “it's more accurate to think about fandom as [being] horizontal. The more sports one follows, the more likely they are to follow the next sport. Fandom is like a muscle [in that regard]. Think about it this way: would it be easier to sell an NBA fan on another version of basketball or convince someone who isn't interested in basketball to start loving the game? Of course, the [former] is more likely to opt into another [league]." While the demographics Engelbert cited are certainly represented within the WNBA fan base, they only account for a portion of the total opportunity. And just because a women’s team’s season-ticket holder has never owned seats to the NBA franchise in the local market, doesn’t mean that he or she isn’t a fan of the team or men’s league. "The majority of WNBA fans, those who attend [and] watch, are people engaging with the major sports leagues,” Valenta said. He would know. He and Fans Have More Friends co-author David Sikorjak recently conducted a study that surveyed more than 84,000 respondents, including ~17,000 self-identifying WNBA fans. 84% of those individuals reported watching NFL games and 83% said they tuned in for NBA games at least a few times per year. item.title: Pochettino will offer something Carrick never could, it’s exactly what Man United are crying out for
item.description: Pochettino will offer something Carrick never could, it’s exactly what Man United are crying out for One of the many concerns surrounding Manchester United under Michael Carrick has been the team’s persistent failure to run. Indeed, United’s lack of intensity under Carrick has become impossible to ignore. Many have pinned this shortcoming on the training methods employed, after Youri Tielemans revealed in pre-season that the side had undertaken virtually no running work and focused almost entirely on the ball. That absence of intensity has left United unable to press effectively and struggling to defend in quick transitions. In a league where intensity is everything, the result has been a winless run lasting more than two months, an 18th-place standing, and a precarious one-point cushion above bottom-placed Crystal Palace. Carrick is now leaving, and the prevailing belief is that former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino will replace him. What Pochettino Brings to the Table Pochettino brings proven Premier League credentials, elite tactical flexibility, top-tier man-management skills, and a sure touch with the media. He tends to build around the strengths of the players at his disposal, as he did at Southampton and during his early seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, rather than forcing a rigid system on them. He can rebuild culture, foster strong squad cohesion, and extract performances through motivation, just as he has done with the USMNT. Above all, though, most United fans will welcome Moises Caicedo’s testimony after he moved from Brighton & Hove Albion to Chelsea. United will have to run like mad dogs Back in 2024, Caicedo confessed: “At Brighton it was all tactical, just with the ball; ‘tactical, tactical, tactical.’ At Chelsea it was run, run, run and it was very difficult for me. With Chelsea I always ran a bit more and with Brighton we almost always had the ball. With Chelsea it was a different football, and we had to run more.” Having watched how sluggish this United side has been under Carrick, and having seen how dangerous they can become when they play with genuine intensity, as they did against Aston Villa , there is every reason to expect a lift if Pochettino implements the same demanding approach. Were he appointed, Pochettino’s high-intensity style might finally cure the Red Devils’ endless wandering. His clear tactical direction would give structure to their running, replacing the raw emotion that has so often seen them charge about without purpose. In the end, under the Argentine, United’s aimless energy would acquire real intent on the pitch, something that, combined with the players’ individual brilliance, could truly hurt opponents. online polls

item.title: Why Scottie Scheffler should be greatly concerned by what Jon Rahm just did on the DP World Tour
item.description: Photo by Warren Little/Getty Images Jon Rahm is back on the DP World Tour, and back to his best. The former world number one hasn’t been the same player since joining LIV Golf, but the moment he left, he was back to his brilliant best. In his first event since LIV’s official demise, Rahm won his first DP World Tour event since 2022. His victory at the Abu Dhabi Championship marked the start of a new chapter in Rahm’s career, and that should deeply concern the current best player alive, Scottie Scheffler. Why Jon Rahm’s recent win should concern Scottie Scheffler Scottie Scheffler has established himself as the undisputed best player in the world in recent years. He’s won 18 times in the last three seasons, including three major championships. A chasm separates him from the world number two. Scheffler’s dominance is like nothing we have seen since Tiger Woods’ prime, but he does have one key advantage over Woods. His historic stretch has perfectly coincided with the creation of LIV Golf, which saw many of the world’s best players leave the PGA Tour. With no Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Joaquin Niemann, and Cam Smith to contend with week in, week out, Scheffler has secured a vice grip over golf’s premier tour. It’s easy to forget that Rahm was once Scheffler’s equal. Before Rahm left for LIV, he was a legitimate contender to Scheffler. He won the 2023 Masters to double Scheffler’s major tally, then won three more that season. Unfortunately for this rivalry, Rahm hasn’t been the same player in recent years, but we have now seen the first sign of a comeback from the Spaniard. The moment Rahm left LIV, he looked back to his best, and the same went for Tyrrell Hatton, who was also in contention in Abu Dhabi. If that trend continues, then Scheffler is set to have far more competition for major championships in the coming years than he has in the last few seasons. item.title: “You Can’t Blame People”: Linda Cohn Reacts as Angel McCoughtry Threatens Legal Action Over Caitlin Clark Controversy
item.description: CHICAGO, USA – August 23: Caitlin Clark 22 Indiana Fever is seen after the WNBA, Basketball Damen, USA game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on Saturday, August 8 in Chicago, USA PUBLICATIONxNOTxINxBRAxMEX Copyright: xShainaxBenhiyoun/SPPx Sportspressphoto_SPR214790 ©IMAGO/Sports Press Photo Angel McCoughtry wants everyone to know she never called anyone “ugly.” She only laughed it off and moved on. But fans took that laugh as an insult to Caitlin Clark, and the criticism came fast. So McCoughtry hit back on Threads on Sunday. “So when people lie and say you said something you didn’t or paint a lying picture. Isn’t that a defamation lawsuit?” she asked. Now Linda Cohn, one of the best-known voices in sports media, has weighed in. “I agree you did not you did not call Caitlin Clark ugly, but you laughed and it was an awkward uncomfortable laugh. And you can’t blame people on social media to assume that you don’t think she’s pretty,” Cohn spoke about it on her show after reading McCoughtry’s post . “And why are we even talking about it? You are a woman. You were a great basketball player for the WNBA. And I know I know when you played, I’m sure you weren’t a fan of people talking about your looks or people’s looks. It just it just this whole thing went went nuts. I just couldn’t believe it,” Cohn added. A legal threat is reshaping the conversation around rookie hype and veteran respect in women's basketball. Subscribe to stay informed as this pivotal moment unfolds. McCoughtry’s legal question came after one viral podcast moment. She was a guest on the Get to the Point podcast with hosts Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer. She said looks and visibility matter more in the WNBA than in the NFL or NBA. To back it up, she told a story about a conference where everyone loved Indiana and Clark, but nobody raised a hand when she asked who knew Kelsey Mitchell. In her view, Mitchell is the best player on that team. Then came the question. Owens asked if she thought Clark was pretty. McCoughtry laughed and did not answer. She went on to talk about Clark’s teammate Sophie Cunningham, who has an Adidas shoe deal even though she scores in single digits, and she asked whether the women’s game is really about talent or “how pretty you are.” Owens pushed back, saying beauty may get a player in the door but can’t make her stay. McCoughtry replied that she wanted the league’s best players to get more attention. The clip passed a million views, and one social media post claimed she had called Clark ugly. She never said that in the clip. So, Cohn’s point is simple. When someone laughs instead of answering, people fill in the blank on their own. From there, more people joined in. item.description: WWE.com A write up from WrestleVotes has fans talking about the prospect of Rhea Ripley's return to WWE television even if she can't actually wrestle. According to the website's recent Q&A session, management wants 'Mami' to come with them on a jaunt over to Australia for the Wrestlepalooza PLE next month. That event is scheduled for the RAC Arena in Perth, Australia on 12 December. Previously, RAC hosted Crown Jewel 2025 . Ripley has been benched since summer with a nasty meniscus injury, but she's on the mend. WrestleVotes added interesting context by saying this: "All signs indicate she’s part of the travelling roster to Wrestlepalooza. Couldn’t tell you if she will get cleared in time. All we know is she’s getting on a plane and getting to Australia. She’s scheduled to travel". That'll be music to the ears of Rhea's fanbase, as well as WWE's creative team. Chelsea Green benefited from Ripley's injury the most: She won a ladder match at SummerSlam to become the brand new Women's Champ , and has rocketed up the ranks as a character generally. It'll be fun to find out what Triple H has in mind for one of his most coveted stars once Rhea returns. She has unfinished business with a belt she never lost, and newly minted heel Tiffany Stratton is waiting with that same title. Via socials, Ripley has asked fans to "stay patient" as she readies for an eventual in-ring return. There's a big, big chance she'll be in a non-wrestling role during the Australian tour/Wrestlepalooza, but people will be chuffed to see her regardless. item.title: Sean McVay admits regret over questionable play call that left Puka Nacua injured
item.description: Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images Sean McVay has admitted he regrets calling a jet sweep that left Puka Nacua with a knee injury during the Los Angeles Rams’ 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The Rams wide receiver was hurt late in the game after taking a heavy hit while attempting to help his team close out the victory. Nacua had already visited the blue medical tent for concussion protocol earlier in the contest, making the decision to give him another carry particularly difficult for McVay to reflect on. Sean McVay takes responsibility for Puka Nacua’s injury after questionable call The incident happened on third-and-11, when the Rams handed the ball to Nacua on a jet sweep in an attempt to secure a first down and run down the clock. He managed only five yards before Jeremy Reaves and Sonny Styles brought him down near the Commanders’ 46-yard line. The impact appeared to twist his right knee and left the receiver on the ground in visible pain. McVay did not hide his frustration when discussing the decision, admitting he had repeatedly questioned whether another play could have achieved the same objective. “I’m kicking myself about those kinds of things,” McVay said, according to Rams beat writer Adam Grosbard. He added: “I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion and maybe ended the game. That would’ve led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee.” Nacua had already recorded 14 receptions for 150 yards before leaving the game, making his absence a significant concern for Los Angeles. He underwent an MRI following the victory, with reports suggesting sprains to his MCL and PCL alongside a turf toe injury. McVay has also indicated that injured reserve could be an option, potentially keeping him out for at least a month. “I’m bummed for Puka,” McVay said. “I feel for him. I feel for all of our players that are getting these kinds of injuries.” With Davante Adams already on injured reserve, the Rams could now face a difficult spell without two of their key receiving options. Matthew Stafford will need others to step up if Los Angeles are to maintain their winning momentum.
